original_question: Let M be a closed surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature. Is it true that, with probability 1, a random geodesic in M eventually enters the subset where the curvature is strictly negative?
target_in_paper: Section 15, Problem 15, "Zero-curvature along geodesics": on a surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature, the task is to show that almost every geodesic meets the negative-curvature set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the ambient object (a genus-2 surface), the curvature hypothesis (nonpositive curvature), the probabilistic/almost-every geodesic quantifier, and the conclusion that a typical geodesic should reach the region where curvature is strictly negative. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to state explicitly that M is a closed connected orientable surface of genus 2.
Since M is a surface, the curvature should be named explicitly as the Gaussian curvature K, with K ≤ 0 everywhere.

The paper leaves "random geodesic" informal; a precise stand-alone formulation should specify how geodesics are sampled, e.g. by choosing an initial unit tangent vector v in the unit tangent bundle SM with respect to normalized Liouville measure.

The event should be stated precisely as: for almost every v in SM, the complete geodesic γv intersects the set {x in M : K(x) < 0}. Your phrase "eventually enters" could be read as a forward-time-only condition, whereas the paper says more neutrally that the geodesic "runs into" the negative-curvature set.

The nearby context contributes only motivation, not extra hypotheses: the paper remarks that there seem to be no known examples of a surface with a nonperiodic geodesic that stays in the zero-curvature set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
refined_question: Let M be a closed connected orientable surface of genus 2 equipped with a Riemannian metric whose Gaussian curvature K satisfies K ≤ 0 everywhere. If one chooses an initial unit tangent vector v in the unit tangent bundle SM according to normalized Liouville measure and lets γv : R → M be the corresponding complete geodesic, is it true that for Liouville-almost every v the geodesic γv intersects the set {x in M : K(x) < 0}?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 15, because Problem 15 is the paper's only statement about a genus-2 surface, nonpositive curvature, random geodesics, and the negative-curvature set. The official formulation is already very close to your draft, so the main sharpening is not to broaden it but to make the implicit measure-theoretic and dynamical language precise: spell out Gaussian curvature, specify the probability space for "random geodesic," and phrase the conclusion as intersection with {K < 0}. The only nearby contextual remark is the observation that no examples seem to be known of a nonperiodic geodesic entirely contained in the zero-curvature set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))
